Project description
Developing Hazard puts an AI through the hazard perception part of the UK driving theory test. It streams PIE dashcam clips from the VAST index and clicks when it spots a developing hazard. Each click is scored with the official DVSA rules: up to 5 points per hazard, more for spotting it earlier, and zero for clicking non-stop.

hasPart.name: Technical architecture
hasPart.description: PIE dashcam clips sit in the VAST index. The VAST pipeline runs YOLO, Cosmos Reason and Cosmos Embed and stores what they find. Our agent reads those stored detections and captions frame by frame at 5 fps, and an LLM on W&B serverless inference decides when a hazard begins. The DVSA scorer marks every click. Runs are traced in Weave and saved as JSON, and the leaderboard is built from a frozen test set. The app ships as a snapshot under 1 MB, deployed on the VAST workshop pod.

hasPart.name: Setup instructions
hasPart.description: Clone the repo onto a VAST Builders VM, copy config.example to .env, add your VSS and WANDB keys, run pytest tests, then deploy with /deploy-app-no-registry.

hasPart.name: Lessons learned
hasPart.description: Three Cursor agents worked in parallel, each with its own spec, and a gate checked every PR. That kept main green across 40+ PRs. The hard part was the human work, not the code: a second labelling pass got blocked by a bug, so we froze the test set with one labeller and said so openly. Size limits on the deploy pod forced a snapshot budget early on.
